questions.stem: A help-desk tech needs a quick, read-only snapshot of a PC's hardware resources, components, and software environment for a remote ticket. Which tool fits best?
questions.explanation: msinfo32 gives a read-only snapshot of hardware resources, components, and software environment - exactly the 'systems resume' described.
questions.trap: Resource Monitor gives live gauges, not a static snapshot. The keyword is 'read-only snapshot'.

questions.stem: A user complains the machine 'feels slow' and you want a live dashboard of which applications are using how much CPU, memory, disk, and network in real time. Which tool?
questions.explanation: Resource Monitor shows live gauges of CPU, memory, disk, and network usage per application in real time.
questions.trap: msinfo32 is a static snapshot, not real-time gauges. Event Viewer logs historical events.

questions.stem: Which keyboard shortcut opens Task Manager directly without a menu?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager directly. The transcript calls this out specifically.
questions.trap: Ctrl + Alt + Del opens a security menu where Task Manager is one option; it's an extra click.

questions.stem: A PC takes 4 minutes to reach the desktop after sign-in because too many third-party apps launch on startup. Which Task Manager tab is the right place to disable them?
questions.explanation: Task Manager's Startup tab is where you disable apps from launching at login to fix slow boot times.
questions.trap: Disabling an app on the Processes tab only ends the current instance; it does not stop it from auto-starting next reboot.

questions.stem: A technician needs to configure safe boot options for the next reboot and control which services start with Windows. Which tool?
questions.explanation: System Configuration (msconfig.exe) controls the boot process, including safe boot options and startup services.
questions.trap: Task Manager's Startup tab disables startup APPS, but boot-level options like safe boot live in msconfig.

questions.stem: Tools such as Event Viewer (eventvwr.msc), Device Manager (devmgmt.msc), and Performance Monitor (perfmon.msc) are most accurately described as:

choices.text: Standalone EXE utilities unrelated to each other
Pure command-line tools requiring an elevated prompt
Snap-ins that can be added to an empty MMC console

questions.explanation: MMC (Microsoft Management Console) starts as an empty shell; admins add snap-ins like Event Viewer, Device Manager, and Performance Monitor to build a custom toolkit.
questions.trap: They're often opened directly by name, which makes them feel standalone - but architecturally they're MMC snap-ins.

questions.stem: A junior tech runs Disk Defragmenter on a laptop with an SSD. Why is this a problem?

choices.text: Defrag is only available on Windows Server, so it will fail to launch
Defrag is unnecessary on SSDs and can reduce the drive's lifespan due to extra writes
Defrag requires BitLocker to be disabled first
Defrag will format the drive without warning

questions.explanation: Defragmentation is for traditional spinning hard drives. On an SSD it provides no benefit and the extra writes shorten the drive's lifespan.
questions.trap: Modern Windows recognizes SSDs and avoids defrag automatically, but a tech manually forcing it is exactly the wrong move.

questions.stem: A USB Wi-Fi adapter is not working and the tech wants to update or roll back its driver. Which tool is the right starting point?
questions.explanation: Device Manager is the hardware roster - it lists installed devices and is where you update, disable, or uninstall drivers.
questions.trap: Disk Management handles storage volumes, not device drivers.

questions.stem: Before editing the Windows Registry, what is the single most important precaution?

choices.text: Back up the affected registry hive before making changes
Switch the user to a Standard account before launching regedit

questions.explanation: Always back up the registry hive before editing. The registry is the central brain of Windows; bad edits can cripple the system.
questions.trap: Running as a Standard user actually prevents most registry edits; you still need backups even when elevated.

questions.stem: A server is having intermittent slowdowns over the course of a week. Which tool is built to track many system metrics over days or weeks for analysis later?
questions.explanation: Performance Monitor is built for long-term metric logging over days or weeks - the right tool for diagnosing intermittent issues.
questions.trap: Task Manager's Performance tab is a 60-second view; it can't track trends over a week.
